headline: Every major above its 200-day line and stretched into overbought, while whales quietly walk coins onto exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because today it is almost unanimous: six of the seven assets on the board, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, and DOGE, sit above their 200-day moving averages. Only ADA trades below its 200-day, some 76.2% off its 12-month high, the laggard of the group. That is a market where the dominant trend is up, not scattered. But 'above the 200-day' after a run like this needs context: BTC is still 38.3% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is 50% off its own peak, SOL is 62.5% off. This is a recovery move inside a longer drawdown, not a fresh all-time-high breakout.

Momentum is where the story turns interesting. RSI-14 readings across the board are hot: XRP at 85.7, SOL at 79.8, BTC at 79.6, BNB at 82.8, DOGE at 77.8, ETH at 76.6. Every one of those sits deep in overbought territory (conventionally above 70), and MACD confirms the trend is still running (all seven show MACD above signal, including ADA, which is trying to turn up from below its 200-day). So momentum agrees with trend, for now, but stretched RSI this uniform is the kind of thing a chart technician flags out loud: it says the move has been fast and crowded, not that it is due to reverse. The 24-hour prices tell a small divergence story of their own: BTC, ETH, SOL, DOGE, and ADA are all red today (ETH down 4.23%, the hardest hit) even as weekly and monthly changes remain strongly positive (ETH +28.26% over 7 days, XRP +47.22%). A hot RSI cooling off with a red day is normal digestion, not a trend break, but it is worth naming as the first crack in an otherwise one-directional tape.

Positioning adds detail. Funding across BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and DOGE on OKX is uniform at 0.01% per 8 hours (about 11% annualized), which is a modest, unspectacular cost for holding long exposure. That is not the kind of expensive, crowded funding that usually precedes a violent unwind. But the long/short account ratios tell a different story by asset: DOGE at 3.24, SOL at 2.07, XRP at 1.46 all show a long-heavy crowd, and the liquidation data over the last 6 to 8 hours backs that up. BTC saw $15.3M in long liquidations against just $1.7M in shorts; ETH saw $14.3M in longs wiped out versus $4.1M in shorts; SOL was $9.4M longs to $1.5M shorts. Longs are the side getting hurt on this pullback, consistent with a market that leaned bullish into today's red candles.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. Spot ETF demand remains a steady bid: BTC ETFs took in $307.5M net on 21 Aug 2026, part of $1,917.8M over the last five sessions with five straight days in the same direction, cumulative flows now at $53.8B. ETH ETFs added $184.0M on the same day, $692.6M over five sessions, also five days running. That is real, traditional-finance demand showing up in the data. Set against that: whale wallets moved $160.3M net onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, driven almost entirely by ETH, which saw $161.6M net onto exchanges (including a single $110M ETH transfer to Coinbase Institutional) while BTC was roughly flat, $1.4M net off exchanges. Zoom out to the weekly whale series and the picture flips again: the two most recent weeks (ending Aug 15 and Aug 22) both show net inflows to exchanges, $573M and $553M respectively, reversing the two prior weeks (ending Aug 01 and Aug 08) which saw $922M and $484M move off exchanges into cold storage. So the multi-week trend has genuinely turned toward exchanges, not just a one-day blip. Coins moving toward exchanges while ETF desks keep buying is a real disagreement between two forms of demand, on-chain sellers positioning near liquidity versus off-chain buyers still accumulating.

Sentiment sits at 71, labeled Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 72. That lines up with the RSI picture: the crowd feels as stretched as the charts look. Stablecoin float is essentially flat, up just 0.26% over 30 days to $308.5B, so the dry powder on the sidelines is not visibly growing to meet this greed. What to watch from here: whether the weekly whale flow keeps leaning onto exchanges for a third straight week, whether ETF net flows break their five-day streak in either direction, and whether RSI cools without a 200-day break, since a genuine trend change would need ADA-style closes below the 200-day to spread to the six assets currently holding above it.
